desc:
Items arrive one at a time; items[i] = [value, weight]. The weighted median of a set of items is the smallest value v such that the total weight of the items with value at most v is at least half of the total weight (that is, 2 * (weight of items with value ≤ v) ≥ total weight).

After each arrival, report the weighted median of all items received so far. (With all weights equal to 1 this is the lower median.)

items = [[5,2], [1,1], [9,6], [4,1], [3,8]]
{5:2}                           total 2  -> 5
{1:1, 5:2}                      total 3  -> 5   (weight up to 1 is 1: 2 < 3)
{1:1, 5:2, 9:6}                 total 9  -> 9   (weight up to 5 is 3: 6 < 9)
{1:1, 4:1, 5:2, 9:6}            total 10 -> 9
{1:1, 3:8, 4:1, 5:2, 9:6}       total 18 -> 3   (weight up to 3 is 9: 18 >= 18)
answer = [5, 5, 9, 9, 3]
hints: Think of an item of weight w as w copies of its value. The weighted median is then the lower median of that big multiset, but you cannot afford to insert w copies.
Keep two heaps again, but balance them by total weight instead of by count: the lower max-heap must carry at least half of the total weight.
The root of the lower heap is the answer exactly when 2 * (lower weight) ≥ total and 2 * (lower weight - weight of its root) < total. Move whole items between the heaps until both hold.
editorial: Let lo be a max-heap of items with the smaller values and hi a min-heap with the larger ones, every item of lo having value at most every item of hi, and let Wlo, Whi be their total weights. The root of lo is the weighted median when two conditions hold: 2 * Wlo ≥ total (enough weight at or below the root) and 2 * (Wlo - w_root) < total (not enough weight strictly below the root's rank, so no smaller value qualifies). Items with a value equal to the root's value may sit in either heap, which does not matter: the answer is the value.

Insert the new item into lo if its value is at most the root of lo (or lo is empty), otherwise into hi, and update the weights. Restore the invariants with two loops: while the root of lo can be spared (2 * (Wlo - w_root) ≥ total), move it to hi; while 2 * Wlo < total, move the root of hi into lo.

An insertion of weight w changes the balance by less than w, so at most about w items (each of weight at least 1) cross between the heaps, and each crossing costs O(log n). With random or modest weights that is a handful of moves per item, so the running time is close to O(n log n); the worst case is O(n * W * log n) for maximum weight W (here at most 1,000). Space is O(n). Expanding weights into copies would cost O(sum of weights) heap operations for every item instead.
time: O(n W log n) worst case, near O(n log n) typically
solution:
import heapq


def weightedRunningMedian(items):
    lo, hi = [], []  # lo: max-heap (-value, weight); hi: min-heap (value, weight)
    wlo = whi = 0
    out = []
    for v, w in items:
        if not lo or v <= -lo[0][0]:
            heapq.heappush(lo, (-v, w))
            wlo += w
        else:
            heapq.heappush(hi, (v, w))
            whi += w
        total = wlo + whi
        while 2 * (wlo - lo[0][1]) >= total:
            nv, ww = heapq.heappop(lo)
            heapq.heappush(hi, (-nv, ww))
            wlo -= ww
            whi += ww
        while 2 * wlo < total:
            vv, ww = heapq.heappop(hi)
            heapq.heappush(lo, (-vv, ww))
            whi -= ww
            wlo += ww
        out.append(-lo[0][0])
    return out
